text:
incident-bot: PAGED @oncall-sre — Sev1: elevated error rate on serving cluster in us-west-2, multiple pods crashing (OOM/CUDA errors) detected by alerting; auto-created incident channel.

oncall-sre: acknowledged. pulling logs now, please add any immediate mitigation ideas here.

ashok: seeing a pattern on the kernel side: repeated IB/RDMA retries then reorder warnings. a few nodes show `rdma_cm: requeue_req` and then `mlx5_core 0000:06:00.0: IB DPORT: excess retransmits`. copying snippet:

```
Jan 23 03:12:54 node-12 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:06:00.0: mlx5_ib: qp 3456: rq timeout, retry 7
Jan 23 03:12:54 node-12 kernel: rdma_repost_send: skb_acked but not sent
Jan 23 03:12:56 node-12 kernel: IB retry exceeded, aborting qp 3456
```

julia: on the serving side we're seeing long stalls in allreduce/collectives between model shards. when RDMA link degrades the runtime falls back/queues and memory for KV cache spikes — some processes hit CUDA out-of-memory during recovery and crash the container. stack traces point to the token-kv-manager waiting on network I/O.

kevin: confirming: metric export shows sustained RTT spikes 100ms->10s between pods on the IB fabric, retransmit count skyrockets. emb-ingest and generation lanes affected.

maria: customer-impact check: product signals show ~18% error rate for text-gen endpoints in us-west-2 over the last 12m; a few high-traffic customers reported failures. customer-support, can you list affected accounts and escalation status?

customer-support: we've opened tickets with 3 enterprise customers (acct-A, acct-C, acct-F). CS rep pinged them, offering mitigation notes and ETA; they want periodic updates.

oncall-sre: immediate mitigation plan suggestion: 1) isolate affected nodes from RDMA mesh so they fall back to TCP, 2) restart serving deploys on those nodes to relieve hung CUDA processes, 3) apply temporary throttling/burst limits to reduce KV cache growth. who can flip the rdma toggle?

ashok: I can. prefer node-level first: we can cordon + label affected nodes and set `RDMA_ENABLED=false` for the runtime daemonset env so pods restart with TCP only. doing a dry-run now. commands:

```
kubectl cordon node-12
kubectl label node node-12 redwood/rdma-disabled=true
kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/rdma-proxy RDMA_ENABLED=false
kubectl -n serve rollout restart deployment/serve-prod-3 --timeout=10m
```

deploy-bot: deploy/serve-prod-3 rollout started by ashok — watch: https://deploys.redwood.internal/serve-prod-3/1856

julia: nice. also recommend enabling conservative KV eviction for the rolling window so OOMs are less likely while we lose ideal network performance. set `KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=3e9` for the deployment.

kevin: reminder: one of the model shards is pinned to node-12 (large GPU), we should relocate or tolerate with padding. if we failover too fast we could cause cold-cache storms.

ashok: relocating heavy shards now: `kubectl patch pod model-shard-9 -p '{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"redwood/rdma-disabled":"true"}}}'` then evict gracefully.

oncall-sre: i'm stepping through the rollout logs. pod restarts are bringing latency down in the affected routes, error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% after first two nodes were isolated. still seeing intermittent CUDA panics on node-15.

ashok: node-15 shows similar RDMA hw errors. marking it for isolation as well. executing same cordon/label now.

customer-support: updated impacted customers, gave ETA 30m, they acknowledged and asked for postmortem.

julia: we're also enabling a temporary routing policy: route high-priority customer traffic to dedicated pool (dedicated-psi) that hasn't touched the IB fabric. adding route override with `route=dedicated-psi` in service config.

oncall-sre: handoff — @ashok will lead remediation for the next 45m, i'll monitor alerts and customer comms. handing off pager to ashok in 15m.

ashok: taking pager. current status summary for the incident channel: 4 nodes isolated, 12 pods restarted, error rate down to ~3.5%, no new OOMs in last 8m. ongoing: rebalancing heavy shards and watching retransmit counters.

julia: posting a quick mitigation gist with the safe flags we used for the runtime:

```
# runtime safe-ops used during incident
REDWOOD_NET_RDMA_ENABLE=false
KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=3000000000
RESTART_GRACE_PERIOD=30
```

kevin: telemetry note — we'll need to correlate kv-cache size with IB retransmit counts in postmortem. opening an eval ticket.

deploy-bot: rollout/serve-prod-3 completed successfully in 6m 22s. no failed pods.

oncall-sre: after 40m monitoring, system appears stable. CPU and GPU utilization normalized, retransmit rate trending down. planning to re-enable RDMA only after thorough manual checks.

ashok: filing a mitigation playbook entry and will prepare a knob to temporarily force TCP across deploy groups via console toggle.

customer-support: customers notified of recovery, two asked for root cause timeline and mitigation steps.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — automatic summary: Sev1 incident closed by ashok. duration 00:31:36. postmortem required.

maria: thanks everyone. action items: (1) postmortem with IB packet-loss root cause + why fallback path led to OOMs (owner: ashok), (2) add KV-cache vs network retransmit dashboards (owner: kevin), (3) add a console toggle for TCP fallback (owner: julia), (4) customer follow-ups (owner: customer-support).

oncall-sre: handing back oncall pager to rotation. I'll join the postmortem.

ashok: agreed. i'll capture kernel dump and hardware vendor ticket details in the postmortem. attaching logs to the incident doc.

julia: we'll also add automated eviction safeguards so runtime doesn't let KV cache grow unbounded during network failures.

incident-bot: follow-up checklist created: https://incidents.redwood.internal/1856001234/checklist

customer-support: will coordinate postmortem distribution to affected customers and provide timeline.

maria: closing channel for now, moving to postmortem doc. thanks all for quick response :heart:
